newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Filipinos get assurances on HK future under China.
newsitem.headline: Filipinos get assurances on HK future under China.

text.p: Hong Kong's largest foreign community, the 140,000 Filipinos who work mainly as maids, received assurances on Monday they would not lose out after the British colony reverts to China in less than five months.

Jose de Venecia, a senior Philippine congressman, said he obtained the assurances during a meeting with Tung Chee-hwa, who takes over as Hong Kong's leader on July 1, when the territory becomes a Special Administrative Region (SAR) of China.
"We had a very constructive meeting with the Chief Executive," de Venecia, the speaker of Manila's House of Representatives, told reporters.

"They gave me the assurances that the new SAR will look after the welfare of our 140,000 Filipino workers," he said. "We did not go into specifics but the general principles are the ones that are important."
Most Philippine workers in the territory are women who as domestic helpers in Hong Kong earn wages 10 times what they would earn for similar work at home.

But ahead of Hong Kong's return to Chinese sovereignty in July, many Philippine maids fear a change in policies and increased competition should more mainland Chinese be allowed into the territory, said Ramon Bultron, a Hong Kong-based area coordinator with the Asia Pacific Mission for Migrant Filipinos.
Being a significant contributor towards the Philippine economy, Manila was also also keen to see that Filipinos in Hong Kong kept their jobs after the handover, Bultron said.
"That's what they (Filipinos) like to hear. Of course, practically they have to look and see if that is really what will happen...after the handover," Bultron told Reuters.
De Venecia said China has given similar assurances to Filipinos working in Hong Kong.

"I had a one-hour session with President Jiang Zemin in Manila one month ago and (Philippine) President (Fidel) Ramos as well, and President Jiang Zemin assured us that China and the new political leadership in Hong Kong will look after the Filipinos in Hong Kong," he said.
An estimated four million Filipinos work overseas, mostly in menial jobs such as housemaids.
